items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Track one might be McCartney and Ringo.

ctx.x: So does unlimited digital tracks necessarily make for better music?

No. No. Because we made great records. The Beatles cut Sgt. Pepper’s on a four-track, I think synced to another four track. And it was the technique, if you had four tracks, track one might be like George Martin with the Beatles. Track one might be McCartney and Ringo. They’d mix the drums and the bass on track one. Track two might be — would be the guitars and the bass mixed together. But you had to get all those levels set before you recorded. And then here’s track one, bass and drums. All the drums. You know…

before they broke up they may have been on a sixteen track. But now when you say does more tracks make it — no. But it just gives you more stuff to put on there and try to filter your way through. And somebody asked me today in this recording class, the sound now as opposed to then. I said well everybody now listens with ear buds through their cell phone or computer, and it has to be compressed so much. And that sound back then — in my home music room I’ve got 1969 JBL speakers this tall, and that’s the way I…
